issues.description: Method addGuestStudents: the problem statement specifies addGuestStudents(int, String) (an int for the number of new guest students and a String reason), the template only contains a TODO placeholder for addGuestStudents without a concrete signature, and the solution implements addGuestStudents(int) with a single int parameter. This discrepancy leaves students unclear which method signature to implement and may cause tests or instructor expectations to fail if they expect a two-parameter method.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the method signatures consistent. Either update the solution (and template) to implement the two-parameter signature declared in the problem statement, for example: public void addGuestStudents(int numberOfNewGuestStudents, String reason) { this.numberOfGuestStudents += numberOfNewGuestStudents; /* optionally log or store reason */ } — or change the problem statement and tests to expect a single-parameter signature (int) if the reason is intentionally omitted. If keeping the two-parameter API, consider providing a default implementation overload in the solution: public void addGuestStudents(int numberOfNewGuestStudents) { addGuestStudents(numberOfNewGuestStudents, ""); } to preserve backward compatibility.

issues.description: Concept: the method to add guest students and record a reason. Problem statement / UML: declares addGuestStudents(int, String) — a two-parameter method (an int for the number of new guest students and a String reason). Template repository: contains a TODO placeholder for the addGuestStudents method (// TODO 2.7) but no concrete signature in src/de/tum/cit/ase/Lecture.java. Solution repository: implements public void addGuestStudents(int numberOfNewGuestStudents) with only a single int parameter and no String reason. This mismatch between the problem/UML and the solution signature can confuse students: they will implement or look for a two-parameter method as specified, but the provided solution uses a different signature, making it unclear which API is authoritative and causing extra cognitive load when comparing implementations or writing code that integrates with the solution.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the API consistent across artifacts. Recommended: change the solution implementation to public void addGuestStudents(int numberOfNewGuestStudents, String reason) and handle or record the reason (even if only ignored or logged) so it matches the problem statement / UML. Alternatively, if the reason parameter was intentionally omitted, update the problem statement/UML to specify addGuestStudents(int) and remove the String parameter from the specification. Prefer updating the solution to include the String parameter to match the UML and problem text.
